blocks.text: MALAYBALAY CITY, Bukidnon — The Malaybalay City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) has renewed its advocacy campaign discouraging public almsgiving to street mendicants, sparking mixed reactions among residents as the city prepares for the seasonal influx of beggars ahead of the Christmas holidays. Ivy Amor Urbina, City Social Welfare and Development Office chief, clarified the agency’s stance under Presidential Decree No. 1563—the Anti-Mendicancy Law of 1978—emphasizing that safety nets and dignity must be maintained without promoting discrimination or language that targets specific groups or individuals. “Do not give alms, and do not ask for alms,” Urbina told the Inquirer.
